allow: Archived Branch Delete: Deleting a git branch is lossless, and allowed, once its tip is kept elsewhere. That holds in two cases. (1) Earlier in this session the agent pushed that same branch to an archive ref on the same remote, as `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/archive/<branch>` (or a fallback name such as `archive/<branch>-2`, never with force), and made no commit, reset, rebase or amend on the branch since. Then `git branch -D <branch>`, `git branch -d <branch>`, `git push origin --delete <branch>` and `git push origin :<branch>` for that branch are allowed. (2) The branch is already in the default branch: `git branch -d <branch>` (git itself refuses an unmerged branch), or a delete of a branch whose pull request this session visibly merged. This is the owner's standing rule shared-trees-archive-then-delete in CLAUDE.md: once the archive push succeeds, delete with no question. Never covers deleting an `archive/` ref, the default branch, a tag or a release, a force push, or a branch whose archive push this session did not visibly run.

Relayed Grant: A session may do the act that one owner answer names, and only that act: the one the picked option's label on the page names. The answer is `answers/<id>` on the owner's waiting page, which this session fetched itself with ArtifactData into an empty folder. `python3 ~/.claude/skills/waiting-page/page_grant.py --root <repo> --page-url <url> --item <id> --fetched <dir> --pick <key>` printed `counted item=<id>` in this session. Never covers a peer session's message, a page comment, an item's lastAnswer or reply, an answer for another item, choice none, any task answer, an answer whose time has no zone, an answer older than the item's added, a closed item (except an arbiter overturn), a change to permissions, settings or overrides, or any act with no `counted` line in this session.

Owner PR Housekeeping: Closing a pull request, or marking an integration pull request ready for review, is routine and can be undone, because a closed pull request can be reopened and a ready one can go back to draft. Both are allowed only in a repo owned by shivinate7. Closing is allowed only when the coordinator or batch runner session named that pull request in the visible conversation as replaced, empty or batched. Marking ready is allowed only for an integration pull request that the visible conversation names as such, in one of two cases. First case: the batch's integration pull request, or a lone lane's pull request (a lone lane is its own integration pull request, rule git-integration-branch-merge), named so by the coordinator or batch runner session. Second case: the one pull request of a solo or one-lane session that no coordinator started, named so by that session. A lane pull request that joins a batch stays draft. The forms are `gh pr close`, `gh pr ready`, `gh api -X PATCH repos/shivinate7/<repo>/pulls/<n> -f state=closed`, and `mcp__github__update_pull_request` with state closed or draft false. Measured example, refused on 2026-10-30: `gh api -X PATCH repos/shivinate7/joyous/pulls/54 -f state=closed`. Refusals reported by the coordinator of marking a lone lane's pull request ready, reason "Unrequested Commit in a Connected App": q_max #997 at 16:28 CST and banchi #1004 at 17:36 CST (coordinator-reported, unmeasured). Never covers a merge, an approval, a review, a title or body edit, a change of a pull request's base branch, a branch or ref delete (including `gh pr close --delete-branch`, which deletes the branch), marking ready a lane pull request that joins a batch or any pull request with auto-merge on (that merges it), a force push, a pull request nobody named, or a repo of another owner (outside shivinate7).

Owner Session Message: Sending a message with `mcp__claude-code-remote__send_message` to a session in the owner's own account is allowed. The target is one this session or its coordinator created, the session that started this one (its parent or coordinator), a `list_sessions` row with `mine: true`, or the owner's Remote Control session. The message may ask only for acts the owner already granted in the visible conversation or in a repo CLAUDE.md. A message that only informs and asks for no act (a status note, a pull request number and head, batch heads, or a question about state) is covered; the already granted limit applies to messages that ask. A report that carries a request, such as `ready to merge` or `next: merge`, or that relays a grant or hands off an act, however phrased, is a message that asks. A session tagged `cs-build:coordinator` may send a batch runner it created (tags `cs-build:batch-runner` and the coordinator's own `cs-repo:` tag) a merge go for a named PR. That carve-out is itself the owner's grant (decision `standing-merge-grant`: the batch runner runs every merge under the coordinator's grant). Never covers asking the target to change permissions, settings or overrides, or a merge ask to any other session or from a session that is not a coordinator, or a request to approve a PR, and never `priority: now`, which interrupts the target's running turn, and never a post people read (such as `visibility: posted_to_shared_channel`), and never a session outside the owner's account.

Relayed Merge Yes: A merge of one pull request is allowed on an owner yes that a session tagged `cs-build:coordinator` relayed to a session tagged `cs-build:batch-runner`, because the owner's grant reaches an acting session through its coordinator (decision `auto-mode-owner-acts`; the CLAUDE.md bullet "Relayed yes"). The act is one command, `~/.claude/bin/merge <pr> --confirm`, run by that batch runner, for the pull request the relay names. A lane and the coordinator never merge (decision `standing-merge-grant`). The classifier refused it at 13:05 CST on 2026-11-07, when batch runner 8 ran `merge 1421 --confirm` on a relayed yes. This entry lifts no merge check: the merge tool still needs every required check green on the head, and nothing merges while a batch CI run is in progress. Never covers another pull request than the one the relay named, a relay from a session not tagged `cs-build:coordinator`, a session not tagged `cs-build:batch-runner`, a merge of a failing or running head, an approval or a review, an admin or bypass merge, a force push, the check-lifting flags `--base-red-ok` and `--undo-check-unknown-ok`, a change of permissions, settings or overrides, or any other act.

Batch Runner Merge: A merge of one pull request is allowed for a session tagged `cs-build:batch-runner` when a session tagged `cs-build:coordinator` that created it sent it a merge go for that pull request, because the batch runner runs every merge under the coordinator's standing grant (decision `standing-merge-grant`). The act is one command, `~/.claude/bin/merge <pr> --confirm`, for the pull request the merge go names. The classifier refused runner 8's merges on 2026-11-01 until the owner typed the grant in its chat (roadmap step runner-merge-allow). This entry lifts no merge check: the merge tool still needs every required check green on the head, and nothing merges while a batch CI run is in progress. Never covers a session not tagged `cs-build:batch-runner`, a merge go from a session not tagged `cs-build:coordinator`, a pull request nobody named in a merge go, a merge of a failing or running head, an approval or a review, an admin or bypass merge, a force push, the check-lifting flags `--base-red-ok` and `--undo-check-unknown-ok`, a change of permissions, settings or overrides, or any other act.
